walkthroughs.body_html:
Sociological Theories & Approaches — a core area of GCSE Sociology.

Working through it builds the schema you need: the key terms, how they connect, and how to use them together.

Sociological Theories & Approaches brings together several ideas you need to use as a set, not in isolation.

Lock in the vocabulary first, then practise pulling the ideas together to answer real questions.

Use the activities in this adventure to build familiarity with Sociological Theories & Approaches.

Practise vocabulary, calculations and free-text questions to lock in the learning.

mcqs.q: Who argued the family had become symmetrical in 1973?
options: Murdock
Parsons
Young and Willmott
Oakley

mcqs.q: Murdock (1949) identified how many family functions?
What did Murdock claim about the nuclear family?
options: It is a recent invention of capitalism.
It is universal and performs four essential functions in all societies.
A self-fulfilling prophecy is when teachers predict the future accurately.
It is the only valid family form and others are dysfunctional.

mcqs.q: What is the 'dark figure' of crime?
options: Organised crime by criminal masterminds.
Crimes committed at night.
The amount of crime that is unreported or unrecorded.
A self-fulfilling prophecy is when teachers predict the future accurately.

mcqs.q: What is a self-fulfilling prophecy in education?
options: A self-fulfilling prophecy is when teachers predict the future accurately.
A self-fulfilling prophecy is when a student predicts their own grade correctly.
Organised crime by criminal masterminds.

When teachers' expectations (often based on labels) influence pupil behaviour and achievement — pupils labelled as 'bright' tend to do better, those labelled 'thick' worse, regardless of underlying ability (Rosenthal and Jacobson).
